approach: This is a pure theory paper with no released code, dataset, or weights, so the plan is to implement Algorithm 1 (BCE) directly from the prose and exercise it on the two contract claims. The implementation keeps a separate candidate p and a LIFO stack R, uses two-sided Test(p, xi) returning ordered verdict pairs, retains xi on (G,G), and on any other pair discards both p and xi and backtracks to the most recently retained chip or sets p = bottom. C1 is reproduced by a deterministic GGBBBGG trace with a fixed arbitrary bad-chip policy that still forces every test to be inconsistent; C2 is checked by exhaustive DFS for n <= 8 over all strict-majority type strings and every Table-1-allowed adaptive verdict branch. Optional early termination and the directed variant are disabled/omitted for the target runs per assumptions A4 and A10.

files.purpose: Package marker so reproduce.py can import the implementation modules consistently.

Define G/B chip types, parse and validate the strict-majority promise g > b, define the two-sided Test semantics, enumerate every Table-1-allowed ordered verdict pair for a candidate/incoming type pair, and provide the deterministic C1 bad-chip policy.

Implement Algorithm 1 as a state machine with candidate p, stack R, one Test(p, xi) per loop iteration when p is not bottom, retain/push on (G,G), discard/backtrack on inconsistency, restart without testing when p is bottom, test counting, incoming-chip counting, and optional invariant checks; include the disabled-by-default Proposition 10 early-termination flag.

Hard-code the seven-chip instance G,G,B,B,B,G,G, run BCE with the fixed bad-chip policy, assert the exact Table 2 flow and final result x7 after exactly 4 Test calls, and return a structured trace record for metrics.

Exhaustively DFS over every length-n strict-majority G/B string for n=1..8 and every allowed adaptive verdict branch, checking that BCE returns a good chip, performs at most n-1 tests, never uses a chip as incoming more than once, and maintains the retained-set and discarded-pair invariants.

Single entrypoint that runs the C1 trace and C2 exhaustive checker, validates the expected values, creates results/, and writes results/metrics.json with all counts, branch totals, and pass/fail flags.

config.trace_bad_answer_policy: bad chips always report B (one arbitrary policy; every C1 test is inconsistent under any bad answer)
config.stack_model: separate candidate p plus stack R (A6)
config.p_bottom_rule: n=1 returns x1; p=None at termination on valid n>1 raises an error (A7)
config.exhaustive_domain: all length-n G/B strings with g>b for n=1..8 (A8)
config.adversary_model: branch over every Table-1 allowed verdict pair at each test, including adaptive choices (A3)

steps: Create the directory structure and use only the Python standard library; no pip installs are required because the task is a pure simulation.
Implement src/chips.py: constants G/B, parse_types, strict_majority_promise, allowed_verdict_pairs(candidate_type, incoming_type), and a deterministic bad-chip policy for the C1 trace.

Implement src/bce.py: initialize p=x1 and R=[], scan i=2..n once, call Test(p,xi) only when p is not bottom, push on (G,G), discard both and pop R on inconsistency, restart with xi when p is bottom, return p, and record tests plus per-chip incoming counts. Include optional invariant checks and a disabled early_termination flag.
Implement src/run_trace.py: run the GGBBBGG instance with the fixed policy, record candidate/stack/test outcome per iteration, and assert output x7 and tests == 4.

Implement src/exhaustive_check.py: for n=1..8 enumerate all G/B strings with g>b, then DFS over all allowed verdict pairs at each actual test, validating final candidate is good, tests <= n-1, incoming count <= 1 per chip, no bottom candidate at termination, and the two proof invariants.
Implement reproduce.py: call the trace and exhaustive checker, collect structured metrics, create results/, and write results/metrics.json.
Run the smoke test on the trace plus n<=4 exhaustive subset; confirm C1 tests=4/output=x7 and the C2 branch enumeration returns pass.
Run the full command python reproduce.py; verify metrics show C1 pass, C2 max_incoming_tests=1, all branches return a good chip, and max tests per instance <= n-1.
Inspect results/metrics.json and compare against the contract: C1 exact integer identity and test count; C2 upper bound and exhaustive branch coverage.
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --smoke runs only the GGBBBGG trace and an exhaustive check for n<=4, printing JSON with C1_tests=4, C1_output="x7", and C2_smoke_pass=true; this proves the Test semantics, retain/backtrack path, and metrics serialization before the full n<=8 run.
intermediate_checks: Strict-majority string counts for n=1..8 should be [1,1,4,5,16,22,64,93], totaling 206; assert these before exhaustive DFS.

C1 trace length is 7; expected stack/candidate events: i=2 push x2; i=3 pop x2 to candidate; i=4 discard to p=None; i=5 set p=x5 without test; i=6 discard to p=None; i=7 set p=x7 without test; final tests=4 and output=x7.
Allowed verdict-pair cardinalities are 1 for (G,G), 2 for (G,B), 2 for (B,G), and 4 for (B,B); validate Test semantics with unit checks.
C2 DFS must visit every valid string and all allowed adaptive branches; assert every terminal state has p != None, chip p is good, tests <= n-1, and max incoming tests per chip <= 1.
Check proof invariants after each step: all retained chips in {p} union R have the same type, and every discarded pair contains at least one bad chip.
Confirm early termination, even-n chip dropping, and the one-directional variant are not active in the target runs (A4, A5, A10).
budget_plan: Total reference budget ~8 minutes: 1 minute setup and directory creation (no installs), 2 minutes writing/unit-checking the small modules, 1 minute smoke test, 1 minute full n<=8 exhaustive run, and 3 minutes validation/buffer. The actual full computation is seconds because it simulates at most 7 tests per branch over 206 strict-majority strings with small adaptive branching.
